content:
I wanted to make a thread for ideas of what to put in a Reviewer checklist (I don't currently have time to sit down and put one together in one go) so thought I would put ideas out there.

I think there are 5 different levels of what needs to be checked

  • Level 1: Subject area - is it related mainstream physics
  • Level 2: Organization - do the lemmas and definitions sit in the right place, is it following the structure of an "API".
  • Level 3: Content - do the definitions look relevant, do the lemmas look useful, are the proofs long or split into nice reusable lemmas. Are any definitions or lemmas trivial rewrites of things already in Mathlib or Physlib (AI seems to really like this one).
  • Level 4: Naming and documentation- do the names of results make sense, can they be understood by a physicist, do they follow the conventions of Mathlib. Likewise for the documentation, is it clear and concise.
  • Level 5: Style conventions- no double spaces, lemma instead of theorem except for the most important results, etc.
Made an expanded version of the checklist here: Physlib#1361
